question: In the pulverized-coal boiler co-firing 20% ammonia, what CO2, CO and NO changes does post-flame ammonia injection give, and what NO change does burnout-zone injection give?
expect: post-flame: CO2 -33%, CO -80%, NO about +88%; burnout zone: NO about +571% (abstract)
rendered:
document title="Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions"

The document states that post-flame injection of ammonia in a 20% ammonia co-firing case gives a normalized ratio of CO2 emission concentrations of -33% and a normalized ratio of CO emission concentrations of -80% compared to pure coal firing. However, post-flame injection also increases NO by approximately +88%. On the other hand, burnout-zone injection of ammonia in the same case causes a much larger NO penalty, approximately +571%.
